chunks: ...a great critical scholar to whom the leadership of the Imamiyya came in his time, prolific in writings on usul, kalam, and fiqh...

key_terms.الْأُصُولِ: usul; foundational principles of Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.رِئَاسَةُ الْإِمَامِيَّةِ: leadership of the Imamiyya; the highest scholarly-religious authority of the Twelver Shia community
key_terms.كَثِيرُ التَّصَانِيفِ: prolific in writings; biographical descriptor for a scholar of exceptional literary output
key_terms.مُحَقِّقٌ: critical scholar; one who investigates and verifies sources with precision

ai.seo_question: What did al-Zarkali say about Sheikh al-Tusi in his biographical dictionary al-A'lam?
ai.summary: This passage cites al-Zarkali's biographical dictionary al-A'lam, praising the subject — Sheikh al-Tusi (385–460 AH), author of Tahdhib al-Ahkam — as the foremost Imami scholar of his era with extensive output across the three core Islamic disciplines. Al-Zarkali's testimony, coming from a non-partisan modern biographer, serves as external corroboration of Sheikh al-Tusi's preeminence in the Shia scholarly tradition.
